discovery: The titanium-doped sapphire laser and self (Kerr-lens) mode-locking, the foundation of modern femtosecond laser science

nominees.name: Peter F. Moulton
nominees.affiliation: MIT Lincoln Laboratory (retired); Q-Peak, Inc., USA

motivation: Moulton's invention of the Ti:sapphire laser (1982) provided a gain medium with enormous bandwidth, broad tunability and excellent thermal properties. In 1991 Sibbett and co-workers discovered that a Ti:sapphire laser could mode-lock itself through the optical Kerr effect, producing femtosecond pulses from a strikingly simple cavity. Together these advances replaced dye lasers almost overnight and became the workhorse of ultrafast science. Ti:sapphire oscillators and chirped-pulse amplifiers underpin femtochemistry, high-harmonic and attosecond generation, optical frequency combs, multiphoton microscopy, petawatt high-field physics and precision micromachining. Several Nobel Prizes rest on these tools, yet the people who created them have never been recognised. This is exactly the kind of clever, enabling experimental work that removes a barrier and opens an entire field, and it deserves the Prize.
